text:
mohit: Quick sync — we need to finalize scope for the 'adaptive pin + budgeted canary' plan. Customers asking for tenant pinning plus cost caps during canary.
annie: High level — two asks: (1) tenant pin by model-version and (2) per-tenant daily spend cap during experiment. Both must be enforceable without adding large infra work.
sam: Agree. Also want clear acceptance criteria so sales can promise to customers. Suggested AC: latency p95 <= 200ms on dedicated tier, no more than 3% quality regressions on eval set, and enforceable spend cap per-tenant in UI/API.
kai: For quality regressions — do we use our current eval harness or a smaller prompt set? We need speed for successive rollouts.
mohit: Use the customer-supplied prompt set when available; fallback to the 500-sample smoke-set we run in CI. Threshold: < 2% drop in top-1 exact-match or subjective QA failure rate.
leah: Edge cases: tenants with long context windows (8k tokens) might blow cost caps even at low qps. Need quota meter to measure tokens in near-real-time and hard-stop when cap hit.
jordan: Implementation idea: routing policy + quota service. When pin is active, route to pinned model. Quota service tracks spend in microbilling units; if spend > cap, route to fallback model with cheaper cost profile and a notification to tenant.
sam: +1. Need rollback criteria: if latency p95 increases > 50ms or customer-visible error rate > 1% for 5m, auto-rollback to previous model variant.
annie: Also require manual canary hold gate: experiment pauses if any VIP customer reports >2 incidents in 24h.
leah: Dev notes: quota enforcement should be eventually consistent but offer hard-stop on token count using token counters in the router to avoid overspend.
kai: Quick config snippet for routing policy:
```
routing_policy:
  pin: true
  pinned_version: "v2026-03-01-a"
  fallback: "v2026-02-21-quant"
  spend_cap_micros: 5000000
  enforcement: hard-stop
```
mohit: Nice. QA plan: staged run with 10 internal tenants for 48h, then 50 beta customers 7 days, then open ramp. Monitor token burn, latency, and eval-regression on rolling corpus.
jordan: Telemetry work: add per-tenant compare dashboard showing baseline vs canary on cost, p95, and eval score. Add alert when any metric deviates beyond thresholds.
annie: Decisions today: (A) scope includes tenant pin + spend caps + auto-fallback; (B) acceptance criteria as Sam listed with 2% quality limit; (C) rollout schedule two-stage (48h internal, 7d beta) — owners assigned.
mohit: Owners: infra -> kai (router + quota enforcement), runtime -> jordan (fallback runtime paths), product -> annie (customer comms + acceptance signoff), eng-sre -> leah (alerts + runbook), adoption -> sam (beta cohort + sales comms).
sam: Risks: quantized fallback may produce visible quality drop. We should include explicit customer-facing messaging and opt-in for fallback.
leah: Runbook notes (rough):
- If p95 > threshold -> pause canary, auto-rollback after 10m if not remediated.
- If spend cap triggered -> switch to fallback and notify tenant via email + console.
- If quality regression > 2% -> hold rollout and run triage with ML team.
annie: Next steps: kai to prototype quota enforcement by EOD Thu, jordan to add dashboard stub, sam to compile beta list, leah to draft runbook. We'll review acceptance signoff next Wed.
deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: canary-config/v1 -> staging at 2026-03-22T15:00Z (dry-run)
mohit: thanks — marking action items in linear and assigning. If any blockers, ping here. :thumbsup:
